title: 36. Numeracy & Number Systems: Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction.
questions.question: Which improper fraction is equal to \(2\frac{1}{3}\)?
questions.explanation: To convert \(2\frac{1}{3}\) to an improper fraction, multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: \(2\times 3+1=7\). Keep the same denominator \(3\). Therefore, \(2\frac{1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{7}{3}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number.
questions.question: Which mixed number is equal to \(\frac{17}{5}\)?
questions.explanation: Divide the numerator by the denominator: \(17\div 5=3\text{ remainder }2\). So \(\frac{17}{5}=3\frac{2}{5}\). The correct answer is \(3\frac{2}{5}\).
questions.hint: Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the whole number and remainder.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction.
questions.question: Which improper fraction is equal to \(3\frac{3}{4}\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: \(3\times 4+3=15\). Keep the denominator \(4\). Therefore, \(3\frac{3}{4}=\frac{15}{4}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{15}{4}\).
questions.hint: Use \(\text{whole number}\times\text{denominator}+\text{numerator}\) to find the new numerator, and keep the original denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number.
questions.question: Which mixed number is equal to \(\frac{23}{6}\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(23\) by \(6\): \(23\div 6=3\text{ remainder }5\). Therefore, \(\frac{23}{6}=3\frac{5}{6}\). The correct answer is \(3\frac{5}{6}\).
questions.hint: The remainder becomes the numerator of the fractional part.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction.
questions.question: Which improper fraction is equal to \(5\frac{1}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: \(5\times 2+1=11\). Keep the denominator \(2\). Therefore, \(5\frac{1}{2}=\frac{11}{2}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{11}{2}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the same denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number.
questions.question: Which mixed number is equal to \(\frac{29}{8}\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(29\) by \(8\): \(29\div 8=3\text{ remainder }5\). Therefore, \(\frac{29}{8}=3\frac{5}{8}\). The correct answer is \(3\frac{5}{8}\).
questions.hint: Write the quotient as the whole number and the remainder over the original denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction in a word problem.
questions.question: A recipe uses \(2\frac{1}{4}\text{ cups}\) of flour. Which improper fraction represents this amount?
questions.explanation: Convert \(2\frac{1}{4}\) to an improper fraction: \(2\times 4+1=9\). Keep the denominator \(4\). Therefore, \(2\frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{4}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{9}{4}\).
questions.hint: To find the new numerator, compute \(\text{whole number}\times\text{denominator}+\text{numerator}\), and keep the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number.
questions.question: Which mixed number is equal to \(\frac{47}{7}\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(47\) by \(7\): \(47\div 7=6\text{ remainder }5\). Therefore, \(\frac{47}{7}=6\frac{5}{7}\). The correct answer is \(6\frac{5}{7}\).
questions.hint: Find the quotient and remainder when dividing the numerator by the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a larger improper fraction to a mixed number.
questions.question: Which mixed number is equal to \(\frac{61}{9}\)?
questions.explanation: Divide \(61\) by \(9\): \(61\div 9=6\text{ remainder }7\). Therefore, \(\frac{61}{9}=6\frac{7}{9}\). The correct answer is \(6\frac{7}{9}\).
questions.hint: Divide the numerator by the denominator and use the remainder as the numerator of the fractional part.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction.
questions.question: Which improper fraction is equal to \(7\frac{2}{5}\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator: \(7\times 5+2=37\). Keep the denominator \(5\). Therefore, \(7\frac{2}{5}=\frac{37}{5}\). The correct answer is \(\frac{37}{5}\).
questions.hint: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator.
